thread:
Alex W: Proposal: extract a 'session-state-aggregator' service to own session assembly, prefix caching, and short-lived KV ownership. Goal is to decouple hotpath session mutation from the inference runtime so we can scale and iterate independently, pay down coupling tech debt, and make rollout safer. High-level tradeoffs: smaller blast radius vs extra RPC hop and serialization overhead.

Maria P: Can you quantify the latency cost? even +5–10ms matters for low-latency routes. Also what telemetry do we add to detect regressions quickly?

Alex W: Good call. Initial estimate: one extra RPC + serde ~2–6ms median depending on proto size, p95 impact depends on fanout. Plan: measure with shadow runs and perf harness; add per-request timing (client->agg, agg->runtime, kv hit/miss). We'll gate by latency SLOs.

Jia L: Important: ownership of the KV prefixes. If aggregator owns prefix semantics, runtime needs a compatible fallback. Suggest we keep a compatibility shim in runtime for reads while writes flip to agg. That reduces risk during cutover. Also we should preserve current cache keys and TTL semantics exactly.

Sam R: Rollout proposal: canary -> shadow -> incremental traffic ramp with automatic fallback. Must have a safety net to fall back to monolith if error rate or latency breach. Suggest feature-flagged routing and an automated circuit that switches routes when thresholds hit.

Leah T: Test & infra checklist: contract tests for read/write semantics, end-to-end integration with auth/tenant isolation, perf harness to run current QPS with synthetic traces, chaos tests for partial failures. I can add a runner that replays real traces for 24h to observe p95 behavior.

Alex W: Example of the simplest feature-flag gate we can use in runtime:
```python
# runtime proxy pseudo-code
if feature_flags.is_enabled("session-aggregator", tenant_id):
    resp = call("session-agg", payload)
else:
    resp = call("session-monolith", payload)
```
We will extend this with circuit breaker logic and per-tenant canaries.

Maria P: Metrics we should emit: aggregator_rpc_latency_ms (histogram), aggregator_rpc_error_{4xx,5xx}, kv_prefix_miss_rate, end_to_end_gen_latency_ms (with path tag), and rollout_traffic_percent. Dashboards + alerts for p95 > baseline + 20% or error_rate > 0.5%.

Sam R: ops-bot note: deploy blocked until: contract-tests passed, perf harness run <= 1% p95 regression, feature-flag scaffold in place, and canary automation ready. Use the existing rollout automation runbook.

ops-bot: CI status: contract-tests pipeline queued (job/contract-tests-3832). No failures yet. Remember to tag PRs with "arch-extract" for traceability.

Jia L: One runtime detail: keep the aggregator idempotent for write retries and make traces carry session_version to correlate. Also add a small local cache in runtime for hot reads to reduce RPCs during canary.

Leah T: I'll own the perf harness + trace replayer. Estimated 2 weeks for spike + perf numbers, then we reconvene for cutover plan.

Alex W: Decision summary: Approved spike (2w) to implement a PoC aggregator, run 24h shadow against replayed traces, implement feature-flagged routing + circuit breaker, and set the safety net alerts described above. Owners: Alex W (arch/coord), Leah T (perf & infra), Jia L (runtime shim & idempotency), Maria P (SLO/telemetry), Sam R (rollout automation). Action items: create RFC PR with design + sequence diagram, implement contract-tests, add metrics + dashboard, schedule canary window. If anything blocks, comment here and tag @sam_r for rollout ops. :thumbsup:

Alex W: Next check-in: 2026-04-04 10:00 PT to review PoC results and decide on phased extraction.
